headline: Learned models recover cell-resolution structure from transcriptomic and spatial data
label: Learned Cellular Resolution Representations
summary: Recent preprints and publications apply learned representations to recover cell-level structure from sparse or indirect spatial and single-cell measurements.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned representations that recover cellular-resolution structure from transcriptomic and spatial data. RECON reconstructs whole-slide profiles at single-cell resolution from H&E images, and CoexpressDeconvolve converts spot-based spatial transcriptomics into integer cell counts without a reference. Halo segments whole-cell boundaries from DAPI nuclear images and transcript density maps, while Cell2space maps scRNA-seq cells onto spatial references. Other items extend the logic to population-level modeling, atlas-scale tree encodings, and multimodal integration, though several address domain identification, annotation, or developmental time rather than resolution recovery. The novelty lies in inferring cell-level quantities from indirect or static measurements rather than measuring them directly.
